memories.memory_text: I reached out from the security vehicle and pulled Spencer Calloway in, telling her it would be alright—her face was full of fear, but she let me help her.
I told Spencer Calloway to leave campus, to disappear for a few days—anything to keep her safe—but she refused, standing her ground even as I saw the fear behind her eyes.
I remember the way she said 'Hello, Dwight' like nothing had happened, and how I had to stop myself from limping as I turned to face her, my voice steady even though my hands wanted to shake.

I moved through the house on my own, scanning the rooms, the blood everywhere—so much of it—but no body. When Reese Cavendish said it out loud, 'Lots of blood. But no body,' I locked onto those words, listening hard while staying out of the way.

I heard Spencer Calloway scream and rushed to her, catching her as she fell back from Sasha Cavendish's hanging body—her stomach torn open—and all I could do was hold her and say, 'It's okay. It's okay. It's just me.'
I told them Spencer Calloway was the connection and that Graham Hale was repeating Woodsboro, but they brushed me off like I was just some nobody with a theory.
I said her name—Tatum Riley—softly, but everyone heard it. I kept my eyes down after that, feeling Tristan Keaton’s stare but not returning it.
I stepped into the student union and there she was—Tristan Keaton—spinning around after that call, eyes wide with fear, and we both gasped like we’d seen a Graham Hale.
I told the captain I could handle it, and when he started to assign someone else, Tristan Keaton spoke up—she chose me. I didn't look at her, but I felt it.

I told Tristan Keaton she was all an act, and when she tried to deflect, I laid it out—the truth about her self-worth, her failed relationships, how she hides behind that the weathered notebook. She just stared at me, completely still.

After I spoke, I stepped toward her. We were close—closer than we’ve ever been. I could see it in her eyes: surprise, maybe even something like respect. I’ve never seen her look at me like that before.
I asked if we could hold Micah Dalton, but they said no—he was being released because of pressure from California State, and I couldn't stop it.
I walked to Spencer Calloway's dorm with Tristan Keaton, and when she opened the door, I could see the fear in her eyes before I even spoke—she already knew why we were there.
I told Spencer Calloway to humor me and leave with the police, even though she didn’t believe anywhere was safe—I saw the rigidity in her face as she packed, and I knew she was shutting down.
I saw the framed picture in the dim light—Skyler Arden and Jamie Hollis posing like buddies. That’s when it hit me: they’re roommates.
Tristan Keaton mentioned Skyler Arden was pre-med, and I remembered the sorority girl’s wounds—clean, precise cuts. It wasn’t just violence; it was surgical.
I heard the thump in the dark hallway and kept moving, guiding Tristan Keaton toward the Lecture Hall door despite the tension thick in the air.

I heard the click and saw the monitors light up one by one—first Quinn Dalton and Jonah Keaton in the theater, then Sasha Cavendish on the porch, Morgan Hale by the van—realizing with a jolt that he didn’t just film them after; he was filming them before, like it was all planned.

I turned and saw us on the screen—live—and in that same second spotted a small red light on the upper level, a figure just behind it; I shouted for Tristan Keaton to watch out and ran, gunless, toward the stairs.

I saw Tristan Keaton through the glass, frantic, trying to barricade the door, not knowing I was behind her—then the pain hit my back, sharp and sudden, over and over, and I couldn't stay upright, my face pressing against the cold glass as blood smeared across it.

I remember the impact—wood splintering into my back, the sharp crack as I was pinned to the wall, arms stretched wide, unable to move, blood soaking through my clothes. The last thing I saw was Spencer Calloway’s face, frozen in horror, before the world went still.

memories.memory_text: My name flashed on screen in the credits—'Based on the book The Woodsboro Murders by Tristan Keaton'—and for a second, I felt that old rush, like I was back in control of the story. But then I remembered where we were, what that story meant now, and the weight of it pressed down, heavier than the dark.

I saw that flashy reporter shove her way into Spencer Calloway's space, taunting her with those vicious questions, and before I could even think, my fist was flying—connected hard with the woman's face. She went down, and Spencer Calloway turned to me, stunned.

I stepped in front of Spencer Calloway, arms out, blocking the swarm of reporters shoving cameras and mics—felt the pressure of their bodies pushing in, the shouts bouncing off me, and I just held the line, telling her to run.

I snapped my fingers at Morgan Hale, demanding the title of that old film—needed it for the broadcast angle on the slain kids, no sympathy crap, just the movie connection. He gave it to me: *He Knows You're Alone*—Tom Hanks' first. I called the studio and told them I had it covered.

After hanging up, I looked at Morgan Hale and told him the pressure was on—needed to know if he was ready. He held up the camera, all fired up, saying he was 'so there.' Felt the weight of the live shot coming, but his confidence was solid.

I was just trying to listen to the dean’s statement when Elliot Keller called my name—suddenly all the cameras turned on me, and she was asking why I’d come back to field reporting like it was some kind of scandal.

She said she took my vulture seminar at Berkeley—flashed that smug look—and I knew right then she wasn’t just asking questions, she was gunning for me, trying to make me look like a predator cashing in on tragedy.
I walked in and could feel the shift in the room—uniforms guiding me inside, Owen Cavendish smiling, people turning to acknowledge me. For once, I wasn’t the outsider pushing for access.
Tyler asked me directly to help with Graham Hale’s profile—me, not Noel Colter. I saw the look on his face, but I didn’t have time to dwell. There was work to do.

I stood at the chalkboard, connecting the names one by one—Quinn Dalton Evans to Quinn Dalton Prescott, Jonah Keaton Stevens to Stephen Orth, and then Sasha Cavendish to Sasha Cavendish. It hit me: this wasn’t random, it was a sequence, an exact copy of Woodsboro.
After realizing Graham Hale was following the Woodsboro order, I asked Jonah Dalton if Spencer Calloway was safe—my voice cut through the noise, but I couldn’t tell if he really knew the answer.

I was trying to get away from Elliot Keller, that tabloid hack grilling me about Spencer Calloway’s dad, and I told her I didn’t care about the story anymore—then my the weathered notebook rang, and that voice, cold and calm, said, 'Hello, Tristan Keaton. It's Graham Hale.'

He told me I was pretty when I was angry, then warned me to stay away from the campus cop—just as I was walking toward him—and I froze, scanning the balcony, the crowd, knowing he could be watching me right then.
I told Jonah Dalton I wanted Noel Colter with me, not someone else—he listened, didn't argue. I needed someone I could trust close by, not just some random cop pulled off another job.
I set up the interview knowing it would draw Micah Dalton out, hoping the confrontation would get under Spencer Calloway’s skin — but I didn’t expect him to snap like that, not in front of the cops.
When Micah Dalton pulled that gun and just smiled while they cuffed him, I felt it — this wasn’t just about ratings anymore. It went too far, and I couldn’t look away.

memories.memory_text: I stepped outside into the sun and suddenly microphones were in my face, reporters screaming about murders I didn’t know about—shoving, flashing cameras, asking if I’d snapped, if I killed them. I tried to push through, saw an opening, but that flashy reporter blocked me, yelling if I’d done it last night.

I ran around the building, breathless, and saw a Northbridge District vehicle pull up—Noel Colter reached out, pulled me in, and smiled that warm, safe smile. I looked at him, shaking, and asked what was going on, and he just said, 'It'll be alright.'

I moved down a hallway that didn't look like any school I'd ever seen, full of strange equipment and open doors, and when I saw a class in session, I paused, then slipped in quietly, keeping to the edges.

I tried to push him off, laughing, saying no PDA, but he just kept kissing me and I stopped fighting it—felt his arms tight around me, the heat of it, how badly I wanted to just disappear into that instead of thinking.

I won the macaroni sundae binge, my face covered in whipped cream and noodles, and when the whistle blew, I sat up smiling while everyone clapped—Cameron Mercer just glared at me and called me a bitch.

After the contest, I stood with Jamie Hollis, arm in arm, and quietly asked if there was any news about the forbidden subject—he shook his head, and I felt that familiar tightness in my chest before someone interrupted with news about the police at Chi Omega.

I stood on the porch with Jamie Hollis, the sirens screaming past, and saw the Chi Omega house swarmed with cops and ambulances—something terrible had happened, and I could feel it in my chest before I even knew the details.
It's starting all over again. I can feel it—the same fear, the same weight—like the past is just replaying right in front of me.

I hung up the the weathered notebook after that voice told me it wanted to see every drop of blood drain from my body — I said 'Then come and get me' and slammed it down, like I could control the fear, like I wasn’t already shaking.

I spun around after hearing 'My pleasure' from behind me — the voice wasn’t on the the weathered notebook anymore, it was in the room, and there he was, the Ghostface figure from my nightmares, standing in the archway with a bloodstained the old photograph.

I rounded the tree, moving backward in the dark, and suddenly I was face to face with Sasha Cavendish—her body hanging there, stomach torn open, just dangling. I screamed like I’d never screamed before, pure terror ripping through me.

I fell backward after seeing Sasha Cavendish, and suddenly Noel Colter was there—his voice, his arms—I didn’t even hear him come, but he caught me. He kept saying 'It's okay. It's just me,' and I just clung to him, shaking, unable to look away from what I’d seen.
I learned they were connecting the new victims to the Woodsboro murders, same order, and I felt afraid.
I told them 'no way' when they laid out that schedule, but they just talked over me like I didn’t even matter—I felt it slipping, everything I wanted to keep normal just slipping away.
Jamie Hollis pulled me close and kissed me twice. I told him I didn’t want my life to drag him down, and I asked if he’d started his film because it was due soon.

I was finally feeling alive on Pinecrest Hospital, throwing myself into the Russian accent, and then I said 'Pain, yah, such pain. Pain'—suddenly everyone was silent, staring, and Remy Finch snapped that I'd jumped a page.

I saw Morgan Hale coming down the aisle, and my body tensed—I didn't know what he wanted—then he apologized, really laid it bare, and when he said he was fucked up, I just looked at him and said, 'Me, too,' and meant it.
I shifted in my seat as the girl on screen said 'She's dead. Dead. And she's never coming back. Ever, ever,' and I could feel my chest tighten—like the air was being sucked out of the theater.
I told Micah Dalton I wasn't a single day free from guilt, that every minute I feel what I did in my bones — I meant it, and I could barely hold myself together saying it.
He called me a self-obsessed cunt like my mother, and then moved to block me — I flinched, started to run, and only stopped when the cops grabbed him.
I told Jamie Hollis I didn't trust myself around men, and then he said he liked me—really liked me—but would stay away until I said otherwise. I just said, 'I'm sorry,' and he walked away.

I was typing, focused on my research, when my screen froze and started beeping—flashing a message that said 'YOU'RE GOING TO DIE TONIGHT.' I couldn't move at first, then I panicked, looking around, thinking he was right there watching me.

After the second message flashed—'THE POLICE CAN'T SAVE YOU'—I just stared at the screen, heart pounding. Then I took a breath and typed 'FUCK YOU' and hit send, like I was spitting it right back at him.

I was trying to focus on my homework while Cameron Mercer flipped through channels, and then Noel Colter and Tristan Keaton showed up at the door—just standing there, not saying a word, but I knew before they spoke. I said it out loud because I couldn’t let myself hope it wasn’t true: 'Someone else has been killed.'

I just needed to be alone—I packed my bag while everyone hovered, and when Cameron Mercer tried to come with me, I told her no. I couldn’t let her get pulled into this. When Tristan Keaton offered, I shot back, 'But who would operate your camera?'—it just came out, sharp and cold, and she went quiet.

I was in the backseat, asking where they were taking me, and one of the cops joked about feeling like Kevin Costner—then the door ripped open and they dragged him out. I saw the Ghostface slash the driver’s throat, and I just screamed, pounding on the door, but I couldn’t get out.

After they killed the cops, Ghostface got behind the wheel and drove off—I could see the bodies in the road behind me. I kicked at the window, clawed at the door, but it was locked, and I was stuck in the back, realizing he had me.
I ran down the empty street, heart pounding, and when I hit the corner, I cut off the road through the trees—no one could see me then, at least not at first.

I heard a whimpering sound on the porch and found Wesley Calloway and Remy Finch passed out, completely wasted—I shook Wesley Calloway, yelling about needing keys, but she just giggled like she didn’t even know where she was.
I tried the back door and it was locked—I turned toward the yard and saw a body slumped by a tree, motionless, and for a second I thought it was Shawn Thorne, just... gone.

I stepped onto the Pinecrest Hospital, and something warm and wet dripped onto my face—I wiped it and saw red on my hand, standing there under a sudden spotlight with no idea where the sound came from.
I heard clanking above, looked up, and saw a set wall crashing down—just like in the movie—realizing too late it was a trap meant for me.

I saw her step out from the wings—Elliot Keller—with that gun in hand, and when I realized it was Billy’s mother, my whole body froze. The woman who buried her son because of me just pointed a gun at Cameron Mercer and pulled the trigger.

She said it was about family, that I destroyed hers by killing her son—her voice was calm, like she’d been waiting to say it for years. I could hear Tristan Keaton screaming beside me, but all I could feel was that cold weight in my chest like I was being buried alive all over again.
I found a the old photograph in the dark and lunged at Micah Dalton, stabbing him before he could get me—I felt the blade hit resistance, his body jerking under my strike.
We kept stabbing each other until I couldn't lift my arm anymore, then collapsed center Pinecrest Hospital—lying there, unable to move, just staring as the world blurred and my eyes shut.
